gen-dafont-stilu-manrope: Blown-glass bowls give Stilu its look. Manrope, a plain sans, keeps a bright gap in every curve, so bump its size up a notch and the text opens out nicely.
gen-dafont-stilu-satoshi: Stilu holds its curves and straights to the same line width, with bowls that swell like glass bulbs. And Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e echo that build, so the two feel cut from one cloth.
gen-dafont-stilu-work-sans: Tall, bulb-shaped bowls and terminals that refuse to curl shut define Stilu. Work Sans follows with a high mean line and c tips held well apart, so paragraphs read crisp and uncrowded.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-literata: VCR OSD Mono stamps out fixed-width, code-style letters with a towering x-height and a lo-fi, retro-tech mood. Literata, a text serif, brings bookish thick-and-thin strokes that soften it.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-paquito: Pure retro-tech, all fixed-width. VCR OSD Mono keeps one stroke width in every glyph, while the serif Paquito, with its tight step from x-height to caps, is what carries confident, friendly text.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-pilcrow-round: Warm and neutral, Pilcrow Rounded sets big counters in a tall lowercase beneath VCR OSD Mono's code-style letters. But its tight letter spacing and curves left open make paragraphs flow smoothly, a gentle foil to the heading.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-inter: Professional is the mood Inter brings under VCR OSD Mono's lo-fi, fixed-width heading. But shrink that heading and its tall x-height gets lost, while Inter's tube-like lines hold up even when the body runs large.
gen-dafont-venera-fs-gambetta: Thinly scattered, modern letters make Venera look airy. And Gambetta, a text serif with wide channels into each counter and gently shifting strokes, would carry a long read with bookish grace.
gen-dafont-venera-fs-recia: Recia, a text serif, has an authoritative look, with light modulation and generous openings at every weight. And Venera does its best work as a clean, widely spaced heading, while Recia is built for sharp, steady reading.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-literata: Hair-thin strokes beside thick ones, with bowls nearly sealed, give Verve its snap. And Literata, a text serif, does what Verve can't, opening its curves wide and keeping thin and thick lines sturdy for steady reading.
